title: OFF-GRID LIVING: Building a Simpler, Self-Reliant Life
description: OFF-GRID LIVING Building a Simpler, Self-Reliant Life What if the life you've been working so hard to afford isn't the life you really want? Have you ever dreamed of leaving behind the stress, expenses, and endless demands of modern life to build something simpler? A life with more freedom, greater independence, and more control over how you spend your time? Off-grid living might be the answer. But where do you begin? In Off-Grid Living: Building a Simpler, Self-Reliant Life , Jason LeSieur shares the real-life journey of leaving a comfortable life in Las Vegas with his wife, Creiz, to build an off-grid homestead in the wilderness of Alaska. With no utility connections and a desire to live differently, they started with a piece of undeveloped land, a canvas tent, and a plan to build their own home. What followed was a journey filled with challenges, mistakes, unexpected lessons, and a completely different understanding of what it means to live a successful life. Part personal story and part practical guide, this book is a realistic roadmap for anyone considering a more self-reliant lifestyle. Inside, you'll discover: How to get started: Determine what off-grid living means to you and create a realistic plan for making it happen. Finding the right land: Understand property size, access, zoning, regulations, permits, and the important details to investigate before buying. Building your own home: Learn how to approach construction, prioritize essential projects, and build a safe, comfortable home without needing to know everything on day one. Living without public utilities: Explore practical approaches to solar power, water collection and storage, heating, sanitation, and everyday off-grid systems. title: The Off-Grid Survival Manual: Step-by-Step DIY Projects for Water, Food, Power, Shelter &
description: The next blackout is coming. This time, have a plan that's already built. An ice storm takes the power for six days. The taps slow to a trickle, the freezer starts to thaw, and the space heater you were counting on is a paperweight. If that scenario keeps you up at night, this is the book that fixes it — not more theory, and not fear for its own sake, but a stack of real projects you can build on a weekend with tools you already own. The Off-Grid Survival Manual is a hands-on build guide for keeping a household running when the usual supply quits. Every project comes with a plain materials list (real sizes, gauges, and fuse ratings), numbered steps, an honest time-and-cost estimate, and a clear black-and-white diagram you can actually build from. No filler. No wall of half-explained ideas you'll never start. You'll build working systems across the five that matter most: Water — rainwater catchment, gravity filters, a solar still, and greywater reuse, so the taps stopping doesn't stop you. Power — size a solar array, wire a 12-volt battery bank safely, and add wind or micro-hydro, with the electrical done right. Food — raised beds, a chicken coop, aquaponics, seed saving, and a solar dehydrator that keep food on the table. Shelter & Heat — a rocket mass heater, a root cellar, and building methods that hold warmth when the furnace won't. Security — a simple family plan and a defensible layout that protect your home without turning it into a bunker. Plus the readiness foundation that ties it together: a family emergency plan, first aid, and off-grid communication. It's written for the capable beginner — the handy homeowner, the weekend builder, the parent who would rather own three things that work than thirty that don't. title: Off-Grid Survival Systems Bible: 30 Complete Builds for Water, Power, Heat, Food and Waste
description: Every build video ends at the shot of the thing working. This book starts there and keeps going. You can find a hundred tutorials for a rainwater system. Almost none of them tell you that brass valves burst before the pipe does, that the freeze comes on a clear night rather than a cold day, or that an air lock at a high point looks exactly like a dry spring from the kitchen tap. That gap is what this book fills. Thirty complete projects across water, power, heat, food and waste, and every one of them carries two sections you will not find anywhere else: what breaks in it , with the season and the early warning sign, and three checks that lead to the actual fault instead of a list of possible causes. What is inside Water. Roof catchment and first flush. Storage from barrels to a buried cistern. Slow sand filtration and disinfection. A gravity line that keeps its pressure. Freeze protection that starts at the valve, not the pipe. A batch solar water heater. Power. Sizing an array against December instead of the annual average. What belongs on DC. Building and ventilating a battery bank. The charge profile your controller is probably getting wrong. Running a generator as a charger. The standing loads that kill a bank while nobody is home. Heat. Stove and chimney to the published clearances. Firewood, moisture and a woodshed that dries. A rocket stove. A solar air heater. Getting heat out of the stove room and into the rest of the house. Food. A root cellar that solves the two-humidity problem instead of pretending it does not exist. A solar dehydrator. A solar oven. Canning off grid. Cold for almost no power. A smokehouse. Waste, site and buildings. A composting toilet without flies or smell. A greywater line that survives winter. title: Living Off the Grid Survival Manual: A Practical Guide to Running a Household Without Grid
description: A family of four needs 168 gallons of stored water to get through 14 days without a city supply, at 3 gallons a person a day. Most households have never done that sum. Living Off the Grid Survival Manual shows you how to work it out for your own house: water, power, food, heat, waste and communication, in plain steps with the arithmetic written out. It is for people who want to stay home through outages and storms, and for people who are moving toward living without a grid connection full time. Every chapter uses a worked example for a family of four, and your own numbers replace it. What you will learn to do Pick your level (outage, partial or full time) and set your own numbers for gallons, watt-hours, fuel and days of food Collect, store, filter and test water, and heat it without the grid Size solar panels, batteries and an inverter, and know what to ask an electrician Keep food cold and cooked, and keep it from spoiling, when the refrigerator cannot run all day Seal, heat and cool a house, and handle laundry, toilets and trash Stay in touch with a radio and a paper contact sheet when phones fail Plan for a cloudy week, a freeze, a heat wave, a storm or a sick family member Follow weekly and monthly checks and a 90-day plan that builds your setup in stages Made to be used Appendix A holds worksheets and logs you can copy: a water budget, an energy budget, a daily log, checklists and supply lists. Appendix B has quick cards for safety, troubleshooting and unit conversions. Simple line drawings show the key setups, a one-page summary of the key numbers opens the book, and a Quick Finder at the back sends you to any topic by page.
